links.outcome: Readability (Flesch Reading Ease, Flesch-Kincaid Grade Level) of ChatGPT radiotherapy responses
links.effect: Both versions were college level: GPT-4 FRES 34.61 and FKGL 12.32; GPT-3.5 FRES 32.98 and FKGL 13.32. Responses were challenging for the general public.
links.quote: Readability scores for both versions were considered college level, with GPT-4 scoring slightly better in the Flesch Reading Ease Score (34.61) and Flesch-Kincaid Grade Level (12.32) compared to GPT-3.5 (32.98 and 13.32, respectively).

links.outcome: Comprehensibility of AI-generated patient information for the general public
links.effect: Readability of both GPT versions was college level (FKGL 12.32 for GPT-4, 13.32 for GPT-3.5), deemed challenging for the general public.
links.quote: Responses by both versions were deemed challenging for the general public.

screen.reason: The study evaluates the quality, reliability, and readability of responses generated by GPT-3.5 and GPT-4 to common radiotherapy queries using expert ratings and readability metrics, but does not test a specific organizational safeguard or deployment practice.
